description.narrative: In the continuity of the Healthy Cities program carried by WHO Tunisia, as well as for the implementation of solutions aiming at waiting for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 11), UN-Habitat Tunisia will bring its expertise in qualitative and innovative co-design for the realization of healthy, sustainable and inclusive public spaces with and for the most vulnerable and marginalized populations. Through the participatory design of public spaces in the informal neighborhood of Hay Hlel excluded from public urban planning policies, marginalized women, girls and children will benefit from healthy and accessible public spaces, adapted to the reality of their needs and the local context. These public spaces will be functional, innovative and implemented in two ways: - With and for women/girls on the theme of valuing their locally practiced economic activity. - With and for children on the theme of access to educational leisure activities that are currently non-existent. Public spaces reconcile the economic and the social, and address the issue of adaptation to climate change by becoming a vector of access to the Right to the City for vulnerable populations of informal settlements and usually excluded from the urban planning system.
